newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-FIRST HOME LEAGUE DEFEAT OF SEASON FOR AUXERRE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FIRST HOME LEAGUE DEFEAT OF SEASON FOR AUXERRE.

text.p: France winger Robert Pires scored two goals, including a brilliant 89th-minute winner, as Metz inflicted the first home league defeat of the season on French champions Auxerre on Wednesday.

Pires's international team mate Patrice Loko struck in the 66th minute to give Paris Saint Germain a 1-0 win away to Nice which, helped by Monaco's defeat at Marseille, restored their six-point lead in the first division.
Pires put Metz, who face Newcastle United of England in the third round of the UEFA Cup, ahead with a penalty in the 13th minute after he had been brought down by Auxerre midfielder Christian Henna.
Auxerre forward Steve Marlet equalised within four minutes from a corner by winger Bernard Diomede, then put the champions in front 13 minutes into the second half.

Senegal striker Amara Traore headed Metz's equaliser five minutes from time and Pires, hitting his fifth goal of the season, made it 3-2 just before the final whistle with an angled shot that went in off the far post.
"Our victory proved once again that a football match lasts 90 minutes," Pires said.
"Auxerre dominated us a bit in all areas during the second half but we dug deep into our physical reserves and managed that way to make up the difference.
"After our UEFA Cup victory over Sporting (of Portugal) we are in a euphoric mood," he added.
Auxerre's furious coach Guy Roux said: "Some of my players forget that football is a job, not a game."
PSG's Brazilian manager Ricardo said: "It's turned into a fine evening for us, since we've won at Nice and we've got a six-point advantage over our pursuers.
"Having said that, it was a difficult match. We knew it would be. We've played three matches in six days, the fatigue was evident. Now we have a very welcome week's rest."
PSG beat Galatasaray of Turkey 4-0 at home last Thursday to reach the third round of the European Cup Winners' Cup, then won a home league match on Sunday 3-0 against Bastia.
Monaco, who lost 3-1 at Marseille's Velodrome ground on Tuesday, remained in second place one point ahead of Auxerre as the bunch of teams behind PSG tightened.

Lille's 2-1 home win over Lens with two goals from forward Patrick Collot lifted them into fourth place, one point above Metz and Strasbourg, for whom Pascal Nouma scored twice in a 2-1 home victory over Montpellier.

Veteran striker Jean-Pierre Papin scored his sixth goal of the season in seventh-placed Bordeaux's 1-0 home win over Cannes, volleying home after midfielder Stephane Ziani's shot came back off the angle of post and crossbar.
Diminutive Bastia forward Wilfried Gohel scored two of the Corsican side's goals in their 3-1 home win against Lyon.
Nancy climbed off the bottom of the table with their first home win of the season, 2-0 against Guingamp, with Nice, who have conceded 30 goals in 16 games, dropping below them.
